/-!
# Erdős Problem 403

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/403](https://www.erdosproblems.com/403)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Li76] Lin, S., *On two problems of Erdős concerning sums of distinct factorials*.
  Bell Laboratories internal memorandum (1960).
-/

namespace Erdos403

/--
Does the equation
$$2^m=a_1!+\cdots+a_k!$$
with $a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_k$ have only finitely many solutions?

Asked by Burr and Erdős. Frankl and Lin [Li76] independently showed that the answer is yes, and
the largest solution is
$$2^7=2!+3!+5!.$$
In fact Lin showed that the largest power of $2$ which can divide a sum of distinct factorials
containing $2$ is $2^{254}$, and that there are only 5 solutions to $3^m=a_1!+\cdots+a_k!$
(when $m=0,1,2,3,6$).

See also [404].

A solution is encoded below as a pair $(m, s)$ where $s$ is the finite set
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_k\}$ of positive integers, so the distinctness of the $a_i$ is
given by set membership. The empty set contributes no solutions since $2^m \geq 1 > 0$.

The linked proof gives more than finiteness: it classifies the solutions outright, as
$(0,\{1\})$, $(1,\{2\})$, $(3,\{2,3\})$, $(5,\{2,3,4\})$ and $(7,\{2,3,5\})$, so the set below
has exactly five elements.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/f8a51976fd2e66a52b4928c109fb9ae877a1a507/problems/403/Erdos403.lean"]
theorem erdos_403 : answer(True) ↔
    {p : ℕ × Finset ℕ | (∀ a ∈ p.2, 0 < a) ∧
      2 ^ p.1 = ∑ a ∈ p.2, a.factorial}.Finite := by
  sorry

end Erdos403

findings.description: The module bibliography, lines 26–27, dates Lin’s “On two problems of Erdős concerning sums of distinct factorials” to 1960. The cited Erdős–Graham book dates this same memorandum to 1976. This is a bibliographic typo, also present on erdosproblems.com; it does not affect the theorem’s mathematics.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős and Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1980), bibliography p. 118, entry [Lin (76)]: “On two problems of Erdős concerning sums of distinct factorials. Bell Laboratories internal memorandum (1976).” Scan: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf, PDF page 114.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “Bell Laboratories internal memorandum (1960)” to “Bell Laboratories internal memorandum (1976)”.

reformulations.difference: Solutions are represented by pairs (m, s) with s a finite set of positive naturals, rather than strictly increasing tuples. There is no explicit nonempty-set hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite set has a unique increasing enumeration of length s.card, and every strictly increasing finite tuple gives such a set; the factorial sum is preserved. Moreover, 2^m > 0 rules out s = ∅ because its sum is zero. In scratch Lean, solution_iff_increasing_sequence proves the pointwise equivalence with an increasing sequence of positive length, and a separate equivalence verifies the linked proof’s predicate, including its explicit Nonempty condition.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization or status issue found in Erdos403.erdos_403. The source records an affirmative, Lean-verified solution, matching answer(True), research solved, and the formal_proof attribute. Boundary tests and exhaustive enumeration for m < 16 with indices in {1,…,10} returned exactly the five documented pairs. The exact linked proof compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. /workspace/review/proof_bridge.lean derives the file’s exact statement from that classification with the same standard axioms; /workspace/review/scratch.lean also proves finiteness of pairs equivalent to finiteness of representable exponents. Lin’s internal memorandum itself was not available; its results and bibliographic date were checked against Erdős–Graham. The reviewed file still matches its committed blob.
